original_finding_preserved.title: Concurrent distinct invoice settlements can overpay supplier and corrupt invoice cache
original_finding_preserved.trigger_and_safe_repro_design: Disposable DB invoice outstanding 100 EGP, source account 1000. Two requests different RequestIds both pre-read 100, each pays 80. Account lock serializes account only; second never refreshes invoice. Ledger receives total160 while invoice stale Paid80/Remaining20.
original_finding_preserved.root_cause: Business invariant checked outside transaction and unrelated account lock; purchase has no concurrency token or invoice row lock.
original_finding_preserved.correction_design: Acquire invoice UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK in transaction before reading outstanding and tracked state; requery supplier invoice ledger under protection, validate then post/cache. Stable lock ordering relative to account and approvals; unique keys remain for replay.
original_finding_preserved.regression_tests: Barrier-controlled two distinct 80 payments against 100 from same and different accounts: one succeeds, one rejects, total <=100, caches equal ledger; same-request retry replays.
original_finding_preserved.counterevidence_and_limits: Treasury lock protects account from negative pooled balance but cannot make stale outstanding fresh. Different IDs legitimately bypass idempotency. No runtime reproduction performed.
original_finding_preserved.independent_challenge: printing_workflows independently traced all listed source paths; counterevidence searched: permission/approval and pooled balance do not prove collected funds, account locks do not refresh invoice outstanding, same-key dedup does not cover different operations. No runtime writes.

citation_error: Original finding FalahDbContext.cs309-328 quotes real source but covers Customer/Delivery mappings, not Purchase. It cannot support absence of Purchase concurrency guard. Correct Purchase/Payment/SupplierLedger mappings277-305 and actual entity20-60 inspected.
reasoning: Purchase configuration has ID and unique receive idempotency, relationships and payment/ledger individual-key uniqueness. PurchaseEntity has ordinary Paid/Remaining fields and no Version/concurrency annotation. Model search IsConcurrencyToken/RowVersion is present on Order/Shift/Approval/Delivery, not Purchase. PayPurchase reads tracked invoice and supplier outstanding before transaction; later account locking refreshes account movements, not invoice/outstanding. Distinct valid request IDs and sufficient source cash permit two stale invoice admissions; independent repeated-request identity protection does not bind aggregate paid<=invoice invariant.
counterevidence: Existing account lock protects protected account from aggregate overdraft. Purchase paid cache is not source of supplier balance. No claim ordinary same-request replay duplicates; both commands require legitimate purchasing authority. SQL provider lock/deadlock execution was not performed.
